title: Declarative Snapshot + Rehearsal Runway for Safe Model Promotions
author: Marin Cho
release_notes: Adds declarative snapshot resources and a rehearsal stage to the rollout API; introduces automated rehearsal metrics gates and a promoted rollback playbook. No breaking changes to existing rollout CRDs; opt-in via new config flag.
description:
Summary: Introduce a declarative 'Snapshot' resource and a 'Rehearsal Runway' stage in the rollout pipeline. The goal is to make model promotions safer by capturing immutable promotion artifacts (weights, tokenizer hash, config), running a controlled rehearsal with real traffic replay in an isolated runway lane, and gating promotion on a configurable set of metrics.
Motivation: Recent incidents show subtle regressions slip through shadow testing when production request semantics differ. Rehearsal Runway bridges shadow->canary by running a short-lived, production-visible rehearsal that exercises serialization, KV cache plumbing, and end-to-end tracing while still isolating user-visible effects.
Checklist:
- [x] Spec: Snapshot CRD + controller design
- [x] Runtime: snapshot store (S3-compatible) and immutability guarantees
- [x] Controller: runway lifecycle (create, rehearse, evaluate, promote/rollback)
- [x] Safety gates: latency, rr (regression rate), correctness score, sample-based hash matching
- [x] E2E tests and integration with existing rollout policies
- [x] Docs and Console UI additions (runway timeline)
Key behaviors:
- Declarative Snapshot: users create a Snapshot pointing to a model bundle and optional artifact signature. Snapshots are stored immutably with a digest and can be referenced by rollout policies.
- Rehearsal Runway: a new stage type in rollout manifests. When a rollout reaches the rehearsal stage the controller:
  1) provisions a runway lane (isolated routing that mirrors production headers but tags responses with X-Rehearsal)
  2) replays a configurable window of sampled production requests (replay source configurable: live-sampler or recent-logs-replayer)
  3) runs user-defined checks and system SLO gates; collects traces and token-level diffs
  4) if gates pass, proceeds to canary; otherwise triggers a rollback playbook and quarantines the snapshot for investigation.
- Automated rollback playbook: on gate failure, controller records a rollback journal with prioritized rollback actions (immediate swap, scheduled drain, notify-on-call with playbook link).

Review thread (condensed):
- Priya Nair: "High-level: solid. Concern: replay fidelity and privacy — did we account for PII stripping in replays?"
- Marin Cho: "Yes — sampler has pluggable scrubbers; default pipeline uses header-based PII exclusion and supports customer-supplied scrubbing hooks. Added note in docs."
- Liam O'Connor: "Runway lanes look expensive. Can we timebox resource usage or reuse warmed pools?"
- Marin Cho: "Controller will prefer warm pools if available; added autoscale cap and timeout (configurable, default 5 minutes)."
- Noah Reed: "We need a clear signal to ops when a rehearsal quarantines a snapshot — how is oncall alerted?"
- Marin Cho: "Quarantine emits an alert to the rollout-alerting channel and attaches a rollback playbook link; created a small PagerDuty integration module (opt-in)."

Post-merge actions:
- Backfilled rollout docs page and console changelog

- Notified SRE to add a low-severity alert for repeated quarantines
Known limitations and follow-ups:
- Replay fidelity depends on available request payloads; some workloads will require custom replayers. Tracking follow-up ENG-9402 to add webhooks for custom replayers.
- Snapshot retention policy is conservative; future PR will add retention lifecycle policies and cross-region replication.
Overall impact: Enables a middle ground between shadow and canary—short-lived, observable rehearsals that catch infra and integration regressions before user-facing promotion.
